video.description:
Learn to explain how to ask SwiftData for exactly the data you need: FetchDescriptor, Predicate Macro & SortDescriptor, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
FetchDescriptor - An object that describes what SwiftData should fetch, with a filter, a sort order and a limit.
Predicate Macro - A macro that turns a Swift condition into a safe filter for a SwiftData query.
SortDescriptor - A value that says which property to sort by and in which order.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain FetchDescriptor, Predicate Macro and SortDescriptor in English?

dialogue.title: Find the right notes

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I need the notes whose `title` is Hi, sorted by `title`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Start with a FetchDescriptor. It describes what you want to fetch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And where does the filter go?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Into the predicate. Use the predicate macro, like `p` in our code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why not write a string filter, like in Core Data?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The predicate macro checks your Swift code when you build the app, so typos become errors.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh, nice. I forgot the sort order, though.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add a SortDescriptor to `sortBy`, like in our code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does the FetchDescriptor also take a limit?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. It can hold a filter, a sort order and a limit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the FetchDescriptor carries the predicate and the SortDescriptor.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Then the context runs it.
A FetchDescriptor holds the filter, the sort and the limit.
